prompt: Draw the data model for my link-in-bio site with analytics: users, pages, links, click events, and daily stats per link.

messages.content: Draw the data model for my link-in-bio site with analytics: users, pages, links, click events, and daily stats per link.

content.text: I'll start by looking at what's already in the project.

input.content:
# Data model: link-in-bio with analytics

```mermaid
erDiagram
    USERS ||--o{ PAGES : owns
    PAGES ||--o{ LINKS : contains
    LINKS ||--o{ CLICK_EVENTS : receives
    LINKS ||--o{ LINK_DAILY_STATS : "rolled up into"

    USERS {
        uuid id PK
        string email UK
        string username UK
        string password_hash
        timestamp created_at
    }

    PAGES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK
        string slug UK "public URL, e.g. /janedoe"
        string title
        string bio
        string avatar_url
        string theme
        boolean is_published
        timestamp created_at
        timestamp updated_at
    }

    LINKS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid page_id FK
        string title
        string url
        int position "display order within page"
        boolean is_active
        timestamp created_at
        timestamp updated_at
    }

    CLICK_EVENTS {
        bigint id PK
        uuid link_id FK
        timestamp clicked_at
        string visitor_hash "hashed IP + UA, no raw PII"
        string referrer
        string country_code
        string device_type
        string browser
    }

    LINK_DAILY_STATS {
        uuid link_id PK, FK
        date day PK "UTC day"
        int clicks
        int unique_visitors
        timestamp updated_at
    }
```

## Notes

- **Cardinality:** a user can have several pages, a page has many links, and a link has many click events and many daily stat rows (one per day).
- **`LINK_DAILY_STATS`** has a composite primary key `(link_id, day)`. It is derived data. A scheduled job aggregates `CLICK_EVENTS` into it, so dashboards don't scan raw events.
- **`CLICK_EVENTS`** is append-only and high-volume. Suggested index: `(link_id, clicked_at)`. Consider partitioning by month and pruning old rows once they've been rolled up.
- **Privacy:** store a hashed visitor identifier, not the raw IP. `unique_visitors` is a count of distinct `visitor_hash` values per link per day.
- **Ordering:** add a unique constraint on `(page_id, position)`, or reorder in the application.
- **Deleting links:** if links can be deleted, either soft-delete them (use `is_active`) or cascade to events and stats.
- **Not included:** page views. If you want click-through rate, add a `PAGE_VIEWS` event table and a matching daily stats table keyed by `page_id`.

content.text:
I've written the data model as a Mermaid ER diagram in `data-model.md`. I haven't rendered it, so I haven't checked how it looks. GitHub, GitLab, VS Code (with a Mermaid extension) and mermaid.live should all render it.

**Relationships**
```
USERS 1──* PAGES 1──* LINKS 1──* CLICK_EVENTS
                        │
                        └──* LINK_DAILY_STATS   (PK: link_id + day)
```

- **users:** `id`, `email`, `username`, `password_hash`, `created_at`.
- **pages:** `user_id`, a unique `slug` for the public URL, `title`, `bio`, `avatar_url`, `theme`, `is_published`, and timestamps.
- **links:** `page_id`, `title`, `url`, `position` (display order), `is_active`, and timestamps.
- **click_events:** one row per click, with `link_id`, `clicked_at`, `visitor_hash`, `referrer`, `country_code`, `device_type` and `browser`. It is append-only, so I suggested an index on `(link_id, clicked_at)`.
- **link_daily_stats:** one row per link per day, with `clicks` and `unique_visitors`. A scheduled job fills it from `click_events`, so dashboards don't have to scan raw events.

**Choices I made that you may want to change**
- A user can have several pages. If you only want one page per user, make `user_id` unique on `pages`.
- I store a hashed visitor identifier instead of the raw IP address, to limit personal data. Unique visitors are counted from that hash.
- I left out page views. Click-through rate needs them, so you'd add a `PAGE_VIEWS` table and a matching daily stats table keyed by `page_id`.
- Decide what happens when a link is deleted: soft-delete it with `is_active`, or cascade the delete to its events and stats.

I can also generate SQL DDL (Postgres, for example) or ORM models from this if you'd like.
